response.why: batch: player A starts

3 lands, T1 Bat (flying evasion + hand disruption vs. Stompy), T1 Go for the Throat removal, T2 flash flier (Mastermind), T4 Kaito finisher. Solid control curve with early plays against a ground-based deck. Keep.

Play Swamp to enable T1 Deep-Cavern Bat (1B flier + hand exile). Bat is my best opening play vs. Stompy: evasive, exiles their best card, and provides early clock. I'll cast it in the next priority window after land resolution.
Activate Swamp to add {B} mana to my pool. Then I'll get another priority window to cast Deep-Cavern Bat with that mana. Building toward the T1 Bat play.
Upkeep with nothing to do. Pass to draw step so I can develop my board. Turn 3 and I'm still on 1 land—need to find action after draw.
Draw step—pass to move to main phase. I have 2 Swamps in hand now and need to develop board (still on 1 land on T3 is behind). Main phase coming up.
Play Swamp (T3, need to develop mana). After this I'll have 2 lands to cast Deep-Cavern Bat. Opponent is on 1 Forest with 7 cards—still hasn't developed creatures, so early fliers are valuable.

Cast Deep-Cavern Bat. Flying evasion + hand exile effect is exactly what control wants vs. Stompy. Turn 3 deployment on 2 lands is good tempo. The Bat will exile their best card and chip for 1 each turn.

Cast Go for the Throat to kill Grizzly Bears. The Bears will attack next turn (summoning sick wears off), and my Bat is too valuable to sacrifice as a chump block. Remove the threat now while my Bat continues the hand disruption.
Target Grizzly Bears. Destroy opponent's 2/2 threat before it untaps and attacks next turn.

Play Swamp to untap it next turn. My Swamps are tapped (used Go for the Throat in Upkeep), so I have minimal mana this turn. Develop the land base; opponent has no creatures, so no immediate threats. Pass after playing the land.

Pass. Tapping Swamp for {B} doesn't enable any meaningful spells (no blue sources yet for Faerie Mastermind or Kaito, can't chain spells with bare black mana). Move to combat to attack with Bat. Opponent has no creatures, so unblocked damage while my Bat continues exiling their hand.
Pass to Declare Attackers. No instants to cast in begin combat. Ready to attack with Deep-Cavern Bat for unblocked damage while it keeps their hand disrupted.

Attack-all: chip damage (1) + lifelink (1) = 4-life swing over time, progress toward win. Bat is flying and evasive; even tapped, it's not blocking their likely plays. We have Go for the Throat in hand for any creatures they cast. Attack-none: solid but no progress. Control wants tempo; we need to close eventually, and Sheoldred (in hand) scales with life differential. Attacking is correct.
Already declared Bat as attacker (now tapped). Pass to Declare Blockers. Opponent has no creatures, so attack will go unblocked for 1 damage + lifelink.

Declare Blockers (opponent's priority). They have no creatures to block, so Bat damage is unblocked. Yielding through end of turn since no combat tricks or priority plays remain—my mana can't cast anything meaningfully, and opponent is unlikely to extend the game here.

Opponent's Upkeep/turn. I have no targets for Go for the Throat yet (no creatures on board). Yield through their turn; I'll act when I untap and get priority on my turn. My Swamps are now untapped and ready for Turn 7.

Opponent cast Alpine Grizzly 4/2 (summoning sick, can't attack). I have no targets for Go for the Throat yet since it can't attack. Yield through their turn; on my turn I can decide whether to remove it or play threats. Deep-Cavern Bat is still exiling their hand.

Cast Go for the Throat to remove Alpine Grizzly. It's a 4/2 that will attack next turn for real damage. Removing it now buys time and preserves mana for Sheoldred next turn (the game-winning card). Sheoldred's deathtouch would handle it, but better to remove the threat efficiently and develop our better cards. I can cast Sheoldred with remaining mana draws.
Target Alpine Grizzly. Kill the 4/2 threat before it can attack next turn.

Go for the Throat cast (Alpine Grizzly should be dead). With 2 Swamps left untapped and no good plays with remaining mana (Cut Down can't hit 4/2), yield through end of turn. Next turn I can develop Sheoldred with more land draws. Bat continues exile engine.

Attack-all: +1 life swing (lifelink), -1 opponent life, Bat chips toward 20-turn clock. Opponent has no creatures to block or present threats. Attack-none: solid but stalled. Control wants to close eventually; Bat's flying evasion over empty board means attacking is nearly cost-free. Sheoldred next turn will amplify the life swing math even further (2 life per draw cycle). Attack is correct.

Bat already attacking (declared). No creatures to target with Cut Down. Pass through declare blockers and combat. Opponent has no blockers anyway. Bat hits for 1, life swings to 22/18. Yield through their turn—next turn I'll have the mana/cards to cast Sheoldred or develop further.

I have 4 black mana from untapped Swamps (Sheoldred costs {2}{B}{B} = 4 total). Engine should offer cast option, but doesn't per the menu. Passing—possibly awaiting end-of-combat or end-of-turn from earlier phases to fully resolve. Sheoldred is the game-winning play next available window (drains them 2 per draw, gains me 2 per draw). Will cast when option appears or on next turn.
Begin Combat, nothing to do. Pass to Declare Attackers so I can attack with Bat (unblocked, chip damage continues). Still planning to cast Sheoldred in postcombat main or next turn.

Attack-all: cumulative chip damage + lifelink swing (~4 life per turn cycle vs them). Bat taps but opponent has no creatures. I hold 3 untapped lands for postcombat Sheoldred (4 mana, game-winning). Board control + hand exile (Bat) + superior hand (Sheoldred, Kaito, Enduring Curiosity) means I'm accelerating toward a close. Attack-none: defensive posture, no progress. Attack is correct.

Bat declared attacking (now tapped). No creatures to target with Cut Down. Pass through blockers and combat resolution. Opponent at 17 life after Bat connects. Yield through their turn; my 3 untapped Swamps are ready for postcombat Sheoldred cast.

Play Island. Now I have blue mana (3 black + 1 blue = 4 total). This unlocks Kaito {2}{U}{B} or Faerie Mastermind {1}{U} as options. I'll evaluate casting one next turn or holding for Sheoldred. Island significantly expands my play options and removes dead draws going forward. Opponent at 17 life (3 damage from Bat damage already dealt). Sheoldred is still the ultimate win condition.

Cast Sheoldred, the Apocalypse. I have 3 Swamps (3 black) + 1 Island (1 blue) = 4 mana. Sheoldred costs {2}{B}{B}: I pay the generic {2} with 1 black + 1 blue, then {B} with 1 black, then {B} with 1 black. This resolves to 3 black + 1 blue total, exactly what I have. Sheoldred is game-winning: every draw they make costs them 2 life while every draw I make gains me 2 life. With opponent at 17 life and my Bat still exiling their hand, this is the moment to deploy the finisher.

Sheoldred is game-winning on her own: opponent loses 2 per draw, I gain 2 per draw (4-life swing per cycle). At 23 vs 17, I have a 6-life cushion that rapidly widens. Without attack: stable, guaranteed win in ~7 turns via drain. With attack: same guarantee, but 1 turn faster (1 extra damage per cycle). Marginal edge to attacking—Sheoldred's dominance means the Bat's blocking utility is less critical now, so tapping it for 1 damage closer to lethal is fine. Bat damage becomes 'acceleration toward lethal' not 'critical defense.' Attack.

Game is functionally over. Sheoldred's drain is working: opponent at 14 (lost 2 per draw on Turn 12), I'm at 24 (gained 2 per draw). Each turn cycle widens the gap by 4 life (their draw -2, my draw +2). At 10-life advantage, opponent will lose in ~5 turns via pure drain engine. No creatures to cast matter; Bat continues chip damage but Sheoldred alone is lethal. Pass and watch the game win itself. Yield through their turn.

attack-all (leaf 1) is mathematically optimal. Deals 5 unblocked damage (Bat 1 + lifelink, Sheoldred 4) forcing opponent to 9 life, while I gain 1 from lifelink to 27. Opponent has zero creatures and cannot block. With Sheoldred's drain effect as a guaranteed lethal clock (they lose 2 per draw, I gain 2 per draw), maximum damage output accelerates the inevitable kill by 1+ turn cycle. No defensive necessity exists. Opponent cannot remove the threat engine or stabilize from 9 life within the drain math.

Pass priority. Combat is already declared optimally (both creatures attacking for 5 unblocked damage, dropping opponent to 9 life). No spell improves this outcome. Faerie Mastermind doesn't affect current combat. Cut Down targets nothing (opponent has no creatures). Developing hand now is unnecessary—Sheoldred's drain is the lethal engine. Let combat resolve and move toward victory.

Pass priority. Opponent is at 7 life with no creatures and no board presence. Sheoldred's drain is an unstoppable lethal engine: each turn cycle they lose 2 (draw), I gain 2 (draw), maintaining perfect control of their life total. At 7 life, they die in exactly 4 more draws (2 for them, 2 for me per cycle ≈ 2 turns). Casting Kaito, Faerie Mastermind, or Cut Down provides no acceleration—the game is already mathematically over. Passing is the fastest path to victory.

attack-all (leaf 1) is overwhelmingly optimal. Opponent at 2 life with Sheoldred in play = automatic death on their next draw (loses 2, goes to 0). This is a guaranteed next-turn kill with zero defense available to opponent. hold[Deep-Cavern Bat] (leaf 2) forces 3 life, delaying the inevitable by 1+ turns. hold[Sheoldred] (leaf 3) delays further by dealing only 1 damage. attack-none (leaf 0) is passive and unnecessary. The game is completely won by dealing maximum damage now.

Pass priority. Opponent is at 2 life after attacks resolve. They die on their next draw (Sheoldred drain -2 = 0 life). No spell I can cast changes this outcome. Casting anything now wastes resources for zero benefit. The game is mathematically over.

Pass priority. Opponent is at 2 life on their upkeep. When they proceed to draw step, Sheoldred's drain triggers for 2, reducing them to 0 life and winning the game. No action needed—the victory condition is mathematically guaranteed on their next action (draw).
